name: Primeval History
summary: Creation, the Fall, the Flood and the Tower of Babel (Genesis 1–11). The story of humanity before God's call of Abram.
dateNote: Placed using the genealogies of Genesis 5 and 11 (Masoretic text). Many readers and scholars do not take these as an exact chronology, so no firm dates are shown.

name: The Patriarchs
summary: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph: God's covenant family, from Abram's call to Jacob's move to Egypt (Genesis 12–50).
dateNote: Counted back from the Exodus, 430 years in Egypt (Exodus 12:40) and the ages given in Genesis: Jacob goes to Egypt c. 1876 BC with an Exodus in 1446 BC, or c. 1690 BC with one in 1260 BC. Scholars who hold the late date usually give only a period for the patriarchs, the Middle Bronze Age (c. 2000–1550 BC). The Septuagint and Samaritan Pentateuch count the 430 years from Abraham's time in Canaan (compare Galatians 3:17), which would leave about 215 years in Egypt.

name: Egypt & Exodus
summary: Israel grows into a nation in Egypt, is enslaved, and is brought out by God through Moses (Exodus 1–15).

name: Wilderness
summary: The covenant at Sinai, the tabernacle, and forty years in the wilderness before entering Canaan (Exodus 16 – Deuteronomy).

name: Conquest
summary: Under Joshua, Israel crosses the Jordan, takes Jericho and settles the land promised to Abraham (Joshua).
dateNote: From the Jordan crossing, forty years after the Exodus (Joshua 5:6), to Joshua's death at 110 (Joshua 24:29).

name: The Judges
summary: A repeating cycle of turning from God, oppression and rescue through judges such as Deborah, Gideon and Samson, ending with Samuel (Judges, Ruth, 1 Samuel 1–7).
dateNote: The judges' years added together come to more than the time available, so many of them probably overlapped in different parts of the land.

name: United Kingdom
summary: Israel asks for a king: Saul, then David, who makes Jerusalem his capital, then Solomon, who builds the temple (1 Samuel 8 – 1 Kings 11).
dateNote: Counted back from the kingdom's division in 931 BC: Solomon and David reigned forty years each (1 Kings 11:42; 2 Samuel 5:4), and Acts 13:21 gives Saul forty.

name: Divided Kingdom
summary: The kingdom splits into Israel in the north and Judah in the south. Prophets call both back to God; Israel falls to Assyria in 722 BC and Judah to Babylon in 586 BC (1 Kings 12 – 2 Kings 25).
dateNote: Kings are dated by Edwin Thiele's chronology, the one most study Bibles use; others differ by a few years. Some date Jerusalem's fall to 587 BC.

name: Exile
summary: Judah lives in exile in Babylon, where Daniel and Ezekiel serve, until Persia conquers Babylon and Cyrus lets the exiles go home (Daniel, Ezekiel, Lamentations).

name: Return & Rebuilding
summary: Exiles return to Judah, rebuild the temple and Jerusalem's walls, and renew the covenant under Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezra, Nehemiah, Esther, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi).
dateNote: Ends around Nehemiah's second visit and Malachi, c. 430 BC, where the Old Testament's history closes.

name: Between the Testaments
summary: About four hundred years with no new Scripture, as Persia, Alexander the Great's successors and finally Rome rule Judea. The Maccabees win a brief independence.

name: Life of Christ
summary: Jesus' birth, ministry, death and resurrection (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John).
dateNote: Jesus was born before Herod the Great died in 4 BC, probably about 6–4 BC. The crucifixion is dated AD 30 here; AD 33 is the main alternative.

name: Early Church
summary: From Pentecost, the apostles carry the gospel from Jerusalem to Rome. Paul's journeys, the letters, and John's Revelation close the New Testament (Acts – Revelation).
dateNote: Ends with Revelation, usually dated about AD 95, late in Domitian's reign.
